prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions, and setting. Use specific action verbs and name clear maneuvers; for any motion give horizontal direction first (toward/away/left‑to‑right/right‑to‑left/past) then vertical (upward/downward), indicate the action phase when visible (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing), and state whether motions are simultaneous or sequential. Describe body posture with concrete, camera‑relative terms (standing, slightly leaning forward/back, seated, reclining, crouching, mid‑jump, mid‑backflip, arms outstretched, knees bent) and specify orientation to the camera (facing the camera, in profile, back to the camera). Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (open‑mouthed, smiling with teeth visible, furrowed brow) and identify gaze targets (eyes looking up at the kite, gaze fixed on the camera). For gestures specify exact type, hand/side, direction, and intended target (pointing with his right hand toward the person across from him). Clarify precise spatial relationships, scale, and proximity—positions relative to each other and background elements (next to, behind and below the stage, in front of/over, atop, touching, a few feet/meters apart, clustered closely, in a line)—and avoid ambiguous “above” by using “in front of,” “over,” or “directly above/overhead” as appropriate. State the number and arrangement of people and describe audience posture/attention when visible (seated in rows, a small group clustered on benches, some leaning forward attentively). Describe lighting and shadows with observable cues (bright direct sunlight, diffuse overcast, directional backlight), where shadows fall and approximate direction or length (casting long shadows toward the lower left). Include visible surface textures or effects when present (wet pavement, puddles, splashes, reflections, motion blur, dust). Keep the caption concrete, image‑centered, avoid speculation or subjective judgments, and output exactly one single sentence (no lists, tags, multiple candidates, metadata, or fallback phrases).
